text: In 2012 an Alabama judge described how courts in his own state collected fines from people too poor to pay. He called it a judicially sanctioned extortion racket.
provenance: In 2012, an Alabama circuit judge named Hub Harrington moved to stop the company's practices in a town called Harpersville, and he did not reach for gentle language when he described what he had found. He called it a judicially sanctioned extortion racket.
